utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Prosecution ready to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- to continue the cross-examination. Then, Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Kunjadic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your answer, I take it that you still understand me -- you can hear me in a language you understand. May I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Then please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kunjadic. On Friday, I was asking you some questions about --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- 17. In particular, the source of information that you relied upon when offering your opinion about that particular incident. Do you have with you a copy of the statement upon which you relied, that is, the statement of Fatima Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement by Witness Fatima Osmanovic, I do have it in my version, which I had written before and used during the compilation of the final text of the report. The reason --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. The question is: Do you have with you a copy of the statement? I think you said yes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the material that I have here, I can now -- in the material that I have and that I call the working version, that is, the first version that was done as a result of examining the incidents, there are two statements given by the injured party. And in the case, I used this because what I was primarily interested in were material traces that exist --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. The question again was simply whether you have the statement. And I think you said that you have a working document. Did you put that working document together?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are quotes from the statements. What I did was to take out excerpts, that is, quotes from the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please take out your copy of the witness's statement -- or the victim's statement, the statement dated the 24th of February, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that statement in front of you? Not the working copy but the original statement.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I have that in my material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, to save time, I ask the witness be given the document. For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, Mr. President, this is the statement of Fatima Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have it. I do have it. I do have the statement. It's here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place it on the ELMO next to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, are you able to read that document whilst it is on the machine next to you? Are you capable of doing that at the distance from the machine?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very sharp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you turn sideways so that you are actually seeing the document on the machine. Does that help?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could keep your voice up so that the microphone can pick it up. Do you see in the second paragraph there is the name Rasema, end of the sentence the name Rasema?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please read very slowly - very slowly - from the end of that sentence; in other words, the beginning of the next sentence to the end of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And perhaps the ELMO could be adjusted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I got water and went back home. I heard a sound of shot. Suddenly I felt I was hit by small stone on my face. Immediately I wanted to climb the wall. There was a garage close to the wall. I heard something was hitting on the garage too. I could not climb onto the wall. I felt something --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Stop there. All right. And now, would you read from the beginning of the next paragraph, just the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I waited for the car. One of my neighbours by the name --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please stop. The paragraph above. I think we might have two or three paragraphs in the English language compressed into one paragraph in B/C/S. Do you see a sentence that begins with the words "I found the bullet had entered"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Purely didactically speaking, could Mr. Ierace give us the statement in one of the languages. It might be easier, then we might be able to navigate the text more easier. Thank you, Mr. Ierace, in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have copies, if you think it appropriate, Mr. President. Though it is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's nothing against it when it helps Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think you said you found the sentence. Could you please read the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I found the bullet had entered on the right side of my cheek and got stuck in the left side of my cheek and sinus."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I thank you for that. Now, would you please go to your report for incident number 17.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I read it or ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Do you see -- at least, in the English version at the beginning of the second paragraph you say, "In view of the fact that she stated that in the instant of being wounded, she sensed gravel hit her face," and you go on to conclude that you think she was wounded by a fragment of a projectile. Now, having reread the statement, do you accept that she was describing the sensation of being shot in the mouth, in the face, by the bullet? In other words, it felt like she was being hit by a small stone, rather than saying that she in fact was hit by a small stone or gravel.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I didn't mean that she was hit by a small stone or that the small stone had got stuck in her face. The small stones can be a kind of by-product of a ricochetted projectile. Why did I write this? For the simple reason is because I know that distances, if there's 100 metres in question, then there has to be --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm suggesting to you is that the victim in fact was hit by a bullet and she was describing the sensation --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. The witness was just explaining for technical reasons why he wrote this or that. And to interrupt him while he was doing this does not seem to be acceptable to the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think the problem was whether the witness really responded to the question that was put to him by Mr. Ierace. But since that your question can still be put to the witness, I would say whatever you would like to -- you intended to add previously, please do so and then Mr. Ierace will put the next question to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to say was that the bullet was stuck or part of the bullet, a projectile -- a fragment of the projectile, as I've already explained why we cannot be precise, cannot be accurate. At this point we had no possibility to look at the x-ray and really identify what this was. But I do know that bullets are extremely -- can penetrate very deeply. For instance, a projectile from a machine-gun at 1.000 metres will penetrate a flak jacket or helmet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Now you enter into a more general description of what bullets can do. If Mr. Ierace would like to know that, he'll certainly ask you. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it true to say that when you read the victim's statement and in particular the reference to her sensation of being hit by a small stone, that you interpreted that as a experience by her that she was being hit by part of a bullet rather than a whole bullet?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, coming back to her statement, you read out to us that she said that there was a garage close to the wall and "I heard something was hitting on the garage too." Is it true to say that you interpreted that as her relating that the garage was hit in the same instant that she was hit?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably. I didn't go into details of the statement in relation to this, but this can be understood as it happening at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed in your statement -- in your report you say "in view of the fact that she stated that in the instant of being wounded she sensed gravel hit her face and heard it hit the garage she was standing next to," and then you go on to identify other factors leading to your ultimate conclusion. I suggest to you that that is not the only interpretation that one can draw from the victim's statement. Another interpretation is that the hitting of the garage occurred when she went to climb the wall alongside the garage. Do you accept that that is another interpretation which may be drawn from those words in her statement? I'll read the words again: "Immediately I wanted to climb to the wall. There was a garage close to the wall. I heard something was hitting on the garage too."

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not insisting that what I have written is 100 per cent correct. The reason, because I cannot have a look at the x-ray of the head, so I cannot state, ascertain, whether in the head there was such or such a projectile. But, of course, I allow for the possibility, since I cannot identify the exact location of her injury. But what points to me that this was a ricochet of a projectile is precisely the gravel and the relatively superficial part of either the projectile or part of the projectile which has actually entered her head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "gravel"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gravel, small stones. That is just a by-product. It could -- they could come from the wall which was hit or it could be fragments of the fragmented projectile or something like that. Again, I cannot say for certain what this is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on Friday a number of times you referred to the ability of a person with your expertise to locate with relative precision the source of fire, if there is an on-site forensic examination. If there is more than -- if there are more than -- I withdraw that. If there are two impact points of a bullet, say the bullet entered a membrane, not very dense, and then impacted on an opposite wall. How would you go about locating and determining the source of fire? Could you tell us. And including whatever instruments you would use to do that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I have spoken about this on Friday, as you said. And on the ground, in this case you do a sighting. A sighting is to join the points which enable you to ascertain through an opening or a hole where the source of fire was. But what you also do is to make an assessment if it is possible, you record exactly every point, that is, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. height, the descent of that point, of the trajectory, and then to see everything that the projectile pierced through on its trajectory. If you went through certain obstacle, how many centimetres? If you went through the body, which part -- the tissue went through? Where did it enter the body? And all of these data is then analysed. There are formula which is used to assess the approximate energy of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The hypothetical case I give you did not involve the passage of a bullet through a person. What I'm asking you for is an explanation as to how you would actually go about establishing with precision the source of fire where you have the bullet passing through the membrane, not very dense, and then impacting, say, on a wall. Do you crouch down so the back of your head is against the -- the impact on the wall and then look through the hole in the membrane? Do you get a piece of string? How do you actually do it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That can be done on the ground in this way: With either string or some ribbons or with some other straight items. But what's important is the descent, the angle of descent. That is, the -- how sloping is the angle? What is its degree of descent? That's when we can use from ballistics tables for a certain type of projectiles that you found on in scene of the incident and then you know which projectile has which ballistics characteristics. And then with all that and with the ballistic angle, then you can certainly -- you can very closely ascertain the source of fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't have the remains of the bullet, I take it with two impact points you cannot establish the angle of descent. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What you can do there is the analysis for each bullet and then you say for a bullet of this kind, then it will be closer to the distance. Then it is -- if it is higher energy, it will be further. And then you do a kind of a range of possibilities. There is no other way to do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I suppose the amount of energy depends on how far the bullet has travelled before it impacts on the first membrane. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The energy is dependent on the velocity and the volume of the bullet. But how far it will go depends from which distance it has been fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So let's assume you've taken a piece of string or ribbon. You've connected the two impact points, and you've established on the other side of the membrane an area along that line of sight. What steps do you then take in order to qualify the position on the line of sight in order to establish the true source of fire? You've told us about the tables. What do you then actually do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you look at the point of impact is the angle of descent. When you connect two points, that is not a straight line unless distances are very short. If distances are short, then you can have a very small difference. Them it's an almost straight line. But if distances are greater, then because of the curving of the ballistic curve, then it has to -- it's not that angle. It has to be closer. The distance has to be shorter than what you have seen. Then you make an assessment. You use by assessing the energy of the bullet on the scene of the incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So in answer to the question, you say that you make an assessment. Does that depend in part, if not entirely, on not only the knowledge of the forensic ballistician or investigator but also the experience of the person who forms that assessment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in any case, it does. The easiest operations, like a criminal technical investigations, will depend on the knowledge, as will everything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us about the statements, the fact that you were given statements, I should say. You've told us you looked at some videos. Which sites did you visit? Do you have a list somewhere that you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said something about that on Friday. I don't have the list, but I think I know them by heart. I may forget something. But it was on several occasions that I went, and we practically had a starting point in the sense that we didn't know the locations in Sarajevo, because the streets have changed its names, so we had to identify scenes of incidents and so on. But in any case, I was interested in -- primarily in the parts of Dobrinja and Nedzarici, Alipasino Polje, Vojnicko Polje, parts of Hrasno Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't have a lot of time. If you remember the sites, could you tell us what they were, the ones that you visited.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I started telling you about the sites. I went with a military expert, so I visited Grdonj, Colina Kapa, Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me clarify it. Which incident sites did you visit? We should add that in your report, you talk about a number of incident -- a number of incidents. If you could go through your report and tell us which ones of those particular sites you visited?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness answered, but it hasn't been entered in the transcript. He mentioned Dobrinja quite clearly. This is not in the transcript. And perhaps that is why Mr. Ierace has been so insistent. Could one just ask the witness to repeat the names that he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, because Mr. Ierace does not have -- received an answer to his question. You are describing a number of incidents. Do you remember which of the sites of these incidents you have visited? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can be very precise. I'll read them out one by one. Number 2 I didn't visit; number 3, I didn't visit; Nor did I visit number 4; number 5, yes; number 6, yes; Not number 8; Not number 9; number 10, yes; number 11, yes, I passed through that part; number 13, yes; number 14, no; number 15, yes. I passed down that street; number 17, yes; number 18, yes; Not number 20; Not number 21; number 22, yes. Again, I passed down the street; number 23, yes. Number 24, yes; number 25, yes; Not number 26; number 27, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you missed number 16. But that's the same site as number 17, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was there when the investigator was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you look at any stage at some electronic 360-degree photographs in relation to any of the incidents?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it explained to you that those photographs were taken either directly on or as near as possible to yellow painted markings which had been indicated by either victims or witnesses as the position where the victim was shot? Were you told something along those lines by Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw those photographs. They were taken from the positions where the victims were. These were 360-degree photographs. And in incidents number 5 and 6 this is something I did with our cameraman in order to see the surroundings at the site, and I did that because of the damage that could be seen there. I did see those 360-degree photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you do that in relation to sites 5 and 6 so that after you left the scene you could still conveniently observe what could and could not be seen from where the victims claimed to have been shot, or witnesses where the victim did not survive, in the case of number 6 and 5?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With regard to incident number 5, I did this because there were barricades there and also because a lot of damage had been inflicted on all sides and all heights. There was damage to the entire building, not just at one level. And in the building that was in front of the demarcation line and on the sides of the building. So I was wondering how this damage was caused. I located this to be able to illustrate that there was a large number of hits caused by shrapnel and projectiles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kunjadic, I haven't asked you what was on the photograph that you took, simply whether the reason that you did it was so that you could look after you left the site at what was visible from the relevant point. You understand? And I think you've said that that's the reason you did it. Now, coming back to the sites you visited, we've been given a letter by the Defence setting out the sites that you visited. And according to the letter, you visited site number 26 - that's incident number 26 - but you've just told us that you didn't. Perhaps you could just check that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll check that. 26? No. That incident was in a flat. We didn't visit any flats. We weren't able to enter anyone's flats or to enter anyone's yard either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, just in relation to that, did you approach the United Nations in Sarajevo at the field office to seek some assistance in order to gain access to flats?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this was requested by the Defence, but I don't know why but we weren't provided the necessary assistance. On one occasion -- for a certain number of incidents we were assisted, but later on we no longer received any assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, incident number 24, we were told by the Defence that you had not visited that site, but you just told us that you did. Could you check that one.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did visit that area, so -- I didn't see much because at the time I wasn't able to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's okay. All right. Incident 21, we were told that you did visit it, but you said you didn't. Could you check that. Again, just yes or no. Did you visit it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes. I don't know what I said, but I visited this --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- site. It had to do with incident number 13, and I visited it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you mention in your report that bullets of a particular calibre could be fired by more than one weapon. What about 7.9-calibre rounds? Which weapons could they be fired by?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could be fired from a -- a classical M-48 rifle or from a machine-gun. It could be fired from an M-76 sniper rifle too. It could be fired from carbines, hunting carbines, which use 8 times 57 ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go to incident number 2 in your report. Were you given a statement by -- in relation to that incident by Ekrem Pita?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date of that statement?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 25th of September, 2001.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that statement, does this appear: "I haven't been able to find the bullet which wounded Anisa, but it was a 7.9-calibre bullet"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your report, you say that it's impossible to determine the type of weapon. Given that there's some evidence it was a 7.9-calibre round, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. does that assist you in determining what possible weapons could have been used?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't take witness statements because I don't know what they know about ammunition. I really don't know whether the witness saw what the calibre of the projectile was correctly or not. I really can't assess this. So I consider this to be an unprofessional assessment, which is why I don't say that we should exclude the calibre they say it was. But I can't take their statements into account because that was not something provided to the police later. The projectile was not provided to the police. And if there was such a projectile, it caused damage at the edge of the wall, near the door. And we really don't know what the degree of the damage -- the force of the impact. I said that if a projectile hits a wall, a hard surface, the surface can be destroyed. It can fall apart. Since the wounds inflicted on the witness were not very serious --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The question was simply whether that calibre assisted you to determine the type of weapon. And I appreciate that you don't have any information on how reliable that identification was. But then again, that's the only material that you were initially given, isn't it, witness statements? Is that correct? And that was added to later by further material.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, where you found an inconsistency between material provided to you, you've mentioned that in your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I have been inconsistent, because I explained that the projectile --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. No, I'm not suggesting that you're inconsistent. You've been given some police reports, some witness statements, maybe more than one witness statement. And where you have found an inconsistency, you have mentioned that in your report, the inconsistency in the document; is that correct? Would you like me to take you to an example perhaps to illustrate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. If I have understood you correctly, the inconsistency is in that a material trace which was found wasn't handed over to the organs of investigation. That is what is the most important factor when you are trying to come to a conclusion, because you base all your assessments on material traces. If someone says that he heard or saw something, I can take this into account, but I simply can't say whether such claims are true or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. And your training qualifies you to visit the scene where the shooting has taken place as soon as possible after that event to make your measurements, to locate material traces, and then to prepare a report; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's how one should proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But here we have shootings taking place in the midst of a war, where in many cases to go to the site of the shooting, even assuming that you had all the forensic back-up, could be dangerous and therefore perhaps was not an option. Is that correct, as you understand it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. I don't know what the situation was like with regard to each particular incident, but yes, this is quite possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even in some of -- I think some of the police reports there is mention that it wasn't possible to carry out a forensic investigation because there was continuing fire. Did you see such references?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was mentioned in some reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're left in a very difficult position, that is, trying to find objective corroborating or inconsistent evidence, that, corroborating witness statements or inconsistent witness statement, when you have very little forensic material to go on.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the wartime situation was such that it was impossible to carry out on-site investigations. But this is the basis for me to compile a report. However, I have to point out that certain things, such as traces, wounds, damage, projectiles, et cetera, these things can be collected later on, three, four, or five days after the on-site investigation, after the incident. In cases when only the duty officer went to the site, I suppose that a forensics expert or a specialist team could have gone to the site too. So I understand the difficulty of carrying out on-site investigations in open spaces at times of war. However, I would approach this in a selective manner. I wouldn't say that this is the case for all cases because sometimes this could have been done better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you wouldn't be critical, would you, of the forensic investigators in Sarajevo in the midst of a war with a number of people apparently being shot on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking as an expert here and about traces. I can't talk about matters that are not within my domain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, coming back to incident 3, perhaps to illustrate some of these difficulties. When you gave us your thoughts on it on Friday, you spoke about the difficulty of determining the angle of the -- the body. I suppose you meant the angle of the back in particular in relation to the impact point on the wall in order to determine whether the bullet came at a parallel direction or from a high point and so on. But I put it to you this way: Is there anything that you've seen of that incident which is inconsistent with the possibility that the bullet entered the top region of her back and exited the lower region of her back and then impacted on the wall in the area that she indicated? Is there anything inconsistent with that possibility?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can neither accept nor exclude that possibility. For one reason: I don't know the direction, the channel of the wound, and this is because of insufficient information, whether the entry wound is at the top and whether it goes downwards. So I don't know the channel of the entry and exit wound. And secondly, as far as I could see on the video, the difference between the point of impact of the projectile and the position where the casualty's legs were, this difference is minor. So I don't see how the body could have fitted into that direction, could have been part of that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said on Friday that you assessed the distance between the impact point and the step to be in the order of 30 centimetres, and you said that that should have been measured. Were you given by the Defence a statement of Barry Hogan --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- That statement being dated the 24th of May, 2002, in which he, being an investigator, gave that measurement? Were you given that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it. It may have been shown to me, but I don't have it at this moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I can tell you that there was such a statement served on the Defence in which he indicated that he did measure that distance, and indeed it was 30 centimetres. Now, coming to incident 4. In your report you point out a contradiction between two statements and, therefore, two -- a witness and the victim as to where the shots came from. You say, "The damaged party, Witness G, stated that the shots came from Orahov Brijeg, and the witness Brkanic Hamdo stated they came from Poljine."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given a statement by Hamdo Brkanic dated the 5th of January, 2002?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have that statement here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please go --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But he wasn't a witness who was questioned, but when the distance is almost in the same direction, then it's difficult to determine. That's what I was thinking of. But we could clarify this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed he wasn't a witness who was questioned, but unfortunately your report is based in part on the statements of witnesses who weren't questioned. So would you please now read out aloud the last paragraph of that statement. I should add that I do not mean to be critical of you at all in making that observation. Far from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you read it, could you do it slowly, since the space of speed usually is higher when reading. So would you please read it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have copies should that be required, Mr. President. But it's a matter of four sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's just a short passage, then it would depend on whether any of the -- anyone present would need a written version. But let's first read it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the statements that the victims gave and the witnesses, they said that there were several shots in their direction. They assessed the distance in the direction from which the fire came in different manners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether you had the statement of Hamdo Brkanic dated the 5th of January, 2002. Are you reading from that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It might be faster, Mr. President, if I give the witness a copy.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it. I've got the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please go to the last paragraph of the statement. And does it begin with the words "when I mentioned Poljine"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- so it seems from that passage that there may not be an inconsistency after all between the account of that witness and the victim - do you agree? - as to where the shots came from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, given that you drew to the attention of the reader of the report that difference -- I'll come back to my earlier question. Is that what you have generally done in the report, where you have seen a relevant inconsistency, then you have mentioned that in the report, as you did with this?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What determined my conclusion was on the basis of the first part, where I spoke about the material traces. And in the conclusions, I do not mention the discrepancies that I illustrated in the sense of the difficulty of determining that their action, dependent on the shot. As to whether it's from one part of the village or another, I don't know that. But in the conclusion, I only said that it was not possible to establish what type of projectile had hit the injured party and from which weapon this was fired. But I did allow for the possibility that the firing was done with the infantry weapons, one of the infantry weapons. Now, these discrepancies that I listed, they're just illustrations in a sense that witness statements can be unreliable data. It's just for orientation purposes. That's why I have mentioned this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, just before I sign the redaction in a second, I'd like to go into private session for one --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Second. Could we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your job was to impartially look at the evidence. By that I mean without favour to the Defence or the Prosecution. Is that correct? Bring your professional opinion to the material that you read.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have only worked on the basis of the material traces and what I needed expertly speaking, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that you -- first of all, do you agree with me that nowhere in the report do you comment on consistency between accounts of witnesses or witness accounts and police reports? Nowhere do you say what this witness said is consistent with the police report, what this witness said is consistent with what another witness said. That's not in the report, is it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't reject those reports either. Simply, it wasn't established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that you have mentioned the relevant inconsistencies and beyond those stated inconsistencies, the other material was consistent, although you have not said that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that does not influence my conclusion about the incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not -- perhaps you could listen to my question again. Would it be fair to say that you have mentioned the relevant inconsistencies and beyond those stated inconsistencies, the other material was consistent?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that I have mentioned is in relation to my work directly. I don't see inconsistencies, only in the way that I have written the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In incident 4, you brought out an inconsistency between the statement of Witness G and the statement of Hamdo Brkanic. Your comment on that incident consisted of two short paragraphs, and yet you thought it important, in those two short paragraphs, to make that point. Can we assume where you don't bring forward inconsistencies that you found no others which were relevant in preparing this report? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I do understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is that a safe assumption?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This inconsistency, I mentioned it only because on the basis of sound - and I wanted to stress this - it's very hard to determine a location. That's all. There was nothing else behind this. Everything else is okay. The position of the injured and everything else stands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to incident number 6. In reading the statements, did you understand that the witnesses identified the area where the victim was shot as an area which was repeatedly under fire?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if they're correct in saying that, your observation that there should have been a reconstruction of the incident at the scene was not a realistic option.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was a realistic option.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you think it was a realistic option to have a reconstruction at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A reconstruction of the scene can be done now at this very moment if we know -- because the greatest problem in this incident is not knowing the entry wounds on the bodies of the injured. That reconstruction can be done in relation to that fact and in relation to the statement of the witness who was heard. So without any problems in order to determine its exact position at the moment where that person was shot. It is possible to do that today. That's what I meant when I said "reconstruction."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say without any problems. Given that the victim was killed, it would be necessary, I take it, to find a participant of a similar body shape and height as the victim and that victim would have to stand -- I'm sorry? Go on.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Not just that. But in such cases where a good medical examination has not been carried out, that is, a forensic medical examination, you would have to exhume the victim and to establish its injuries. And with a person of the same constitution, that's not a problem. That is the easy part of the job. But I always insist on traces have to be processed and that these traces have to be included in the part of the trajectory of the projectile. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in your comments to incident number 6, you say it's impossible to say whether she had been hit by one or two projectiles. Firstly, what is the relevance of that, whether she was hit by one or two?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very relevant for the following reasons -- perhaps I'm going to just have to elaborate on this. For instance, the Dobrinja river bed - and that's the first work we did in the photograph that is we took - that's around the river bed of the Dobrinja River. It is sloping. It has concrete sides. At along the river bed, going through Dobrinja, from Dobrinja -- at an angle, and it goes all the way through Dobrinja. So the conditions for ricochetting of the projectile do exist. Now, if the firing is done in such a way that the projectiles go into the river bed and then hit its sides, then the possibility for such a projectile to hit someone else is -- does exist objectively. I looked at the photographs yesterday that you asked me for, and it says that -- and the bridge, when the woman on the bicycle was hit, in fact, the -- it's between Dobrinja IV and where the location where the injured party was. Obviously there was shooting in the direction of the bridge, and one of the possibilities was that the projectile was going in and out of the river bed and that they ended up in the river bed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If she was hit by two projectiles, does that reduce the possibility that she was hit by a ricochetting bullet? Is that essentially what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. What I'm saying: If there are several wounds, it increases the possibility of a ricochet projectile or a defragmented projectile. Let me just explain. For instance, if she has been hit by one bullet - say it's a direct hit - and it was on the sloping side at an angle towards the water. At one point it has -- she has to stoop down. She cannot keep the same vertical position of the body. This is -- depends on the nature of the injury. But she falls down. Particularly if she's been lethally wounded. In order to fire the same bullet, the same location, for instance, a distance of about 1.000 or more metres, the projectile needs more than two or three seconds to get there, to fly there. Under the condition that we fire one and then we target and we fire another one, throughout that time the body has to keep in the same position, so the body has been hit and it's at an angle at this sloping side of the river bed, so it's very hard to assume. This is one of my opinions on -- based on the number of the -- number of the injuries that she suffered at one point and also the inconsistencies. And at one point it said that she's been injured in the head and then it said that she's been injured in the chest. So there is this inconsistency -- or in the neck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One second. According to the English transcript, you said the projectile needs more than two or three seconds to get there to fly --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's over 1.000 metres. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For a distance of about 1.000 or more metres. Are you saying that it takes two or three seconds for a bullet to travel 1.000 metres?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have data here. I can tell you exactly how long each bullet needs. But two -- over two seconds. 2.8 seconds at a distance of 1200 metres, and that is under the condition that the projectile has been fired from a machine-gun or a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that the bullet travels at the same speed regardless of whether it's fired by a machine-gun or a sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They use the same type, M-84 and the M-91 rifle, they use the same type of bullet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd be grateful if you could give us a straight answer to that answer. Are you saying that the bullet travels at the same speed regardless of whether it's fired by a machine-gun or a sniper rifle; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But you just have to be accurate as to which machine-gun. But if it's the same ammunition, then it take -- then it's the same speed, the same velocity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your technical data at the back of your report, you give observations about weaponry and ammunition. Did that all come from your knowledge, or have you derived it from a different -- from another source?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have mentioned this -- I've said this because the Defence has asked me to. Of course, there are some books about -- literature about weapons and basic data, ballistics data is listed along tables.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. The question is simply: Did you get this from a book? Did you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a book. You don't learn that by heart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Which book was it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From these two books. And there's another book, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you included those books in your report, the titles?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in that material, you mention special sniper bullets. You say that the sniper cartridge with universal projectile M-75, due to better ballistic characteristics has a greater precision of fire than a normal cartridge. The sniper cartridge's box is marked 7.9-millimetre sniper cartridge with universal bullet M-75. The bottom of the cartridge is marked with the letter "S." Would you expect those bullets to travel at the same speed as bullets fired from a machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be precise, when I said from a machine-gun, what I meant was machine-gun M-84, which uses the same type of ammunition, the same type of bullet. Also, the mark "S," it means "sniper ammunition." And it is only -- that's only done slightly more precisely. But there are no -- any -- that ammunition for sniper weapons doesn't have any other special characteristics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you understand from reading the material given to you that the victim after she was shot in the chest put her hands on her chest, cried out, and then turned, and then another bullet hit her in the neck, according to eyewitnesses, and she fell down? Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know about that statement. But I don't have the medical report to say whether that is really so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think there was another statement to the effect that after she turned, she was hit in the cheek. This is after she's been shot the first time.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you also understand the evidence to be that some individuals went down to the water's edge, ventured out from behind the protection before she went down, and they weren't shot?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do know about that as well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She went down and she was filling her bucket. And while she was filling her bucket, she was shot the first time. Then she stood up, one assumes, turned around -- or at least turned around, according to the evidence, and was shot twice. Now, do you say that those two impacts would have been ricochetting bullets or bullet fragments?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statements in relation to the wounds that the witnesses speak about, I have to take them with a certain amount of reserve, without the expert report of a forensic physician. And here we also don't have the time differences at the moment when the first one occurred and all the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is much information that we don't have that we would like to have. I agree with you. Perhaps I could I could put it to you another way; is there anything about the incident that rules out the possibility that she was shot deliberately twice?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot rule this out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would that be a convenient time? Perhaps one further thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during the break, if it's convenient, subject to what you are instructed by Their Honours, could you find the source where you indicate the source of the technical information at the back. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Kunjadic, you answered that the sources of the technical information in respect of the rifles was contained in the report. I do understand that Mr. Ierace has some difficulty in tracing it. Could you perhaps during the break identify where in your report the sources of this technical information on weaponry could be found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the report, I mentioned under "References." It's on a separate sheet of paper. I mentioned the book separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just look at the Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has also been handed over. And I also have that in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must admit that I've got a copy here at this moment, just a spare copy. So I don't know whether it's complete. Ms. Pilipovic, this additional sheet of sources was part of the report or ...?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there wasn't a part of the report. That was handed over to the Prosecution, I think, on the 24th or 25th of December in a submission. There are two annexes, and there are -- there is an addition, a slightly expanded, about the literature of Mr. Kunjadic. And I think that this was Mr. Slavenko Terzic. And I think there's a third -- I don't have the submission here with me, but I know for sure this is together with the submission as a response to the Prosecution submission. I think that was filed the 24th or the 25th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, I take it that you'll have a look at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll check that over the break. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then adjourn for half an hour. Could you tell us, Mr. Ierace, how much time you'd still need approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd be grateful if I could be reminded how much time I have left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as my bookkeeping goes, it would be something like 20, 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'd need that time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can use that time. Yes. We'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May the witness be brought into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before that happens, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The time remaining, I think you indicated before the break, was about 20 minutes. The Prosecution requested four hours for this witness and has used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree. We have not finally decided on that. And I was -- when I was doing the bookkeeping, as a matter of fact, I was referring to the time the Defence had used in -- in chief. Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the Chamber has looked with some precision to the time that was spent on experts called by the Prosecution, and that gives a very much -- yes. We've looked carefully to the time used by the Defence and by the Prosecution on experts, and you see there's a great disparity now then. For example, background witnesses, the Prosecution took hardly any time to examine them. On the other hand, the Defence took a lot of time. On technical experts, I would say ballistic experts and military experts, the time was far more in balance. And having taken into consideration also how the cross-examination went until now, the Chamber would invite you, first of all, to see whether you could finish as quickly as possible, but preferably not take more than three hours as a total. And that would mean until now I think you took approximately 1 hour and 40 minutes, so that would be 1 hour and 20 minutes remaining. Please proceed. And as a -- the Chamber has noted that quite some answers of this expert witness might have a more general nature. Very often the point comes back as to what the expertise of this witness could add to evidence which is available in a different way, and there seems to be a pattern of -- where the witness until now on a few incidents has testified that because of the lack of reliable data, that from his expertise he could not support but, on the other hand, also could not exclude certain possibilities. The Chamber wonders whether it would be necessary to do that exercise for all of the incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can assure you I don't intend to take the witness to all of the incidents. And that's something I factored into my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And try to keep within the limits I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I also at this stage just clarify whether there's any issue with the Defence that they were -- they had disclosed to them have a supplementary information sheet in relation to incident 3, in which the measurement of 30 centimetres was given, and indeed later a 92 bis statement from Barry Hogan containing the same information. If there's any dispute about that, I can tender the relevant page. Perhaps if I might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Until now I did not hear any objection against you putting to the witness that it was measured. But if objection would be raised about it, we'll hear about it. And then you might be in a position Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to tender that document if necessary. I don't think it's -- the 30 centimetres as such might not be the core of the problem you wanted to demonstrate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just no relation to incident 6, I think you told us that you had seen a statement by the son of the deceased - and I won't mention his name - in which he spoke of two wounds; is that correct? I withdraw that. In which he spoke of a wound on the left side of the victim's neck and -- that is, a penetrating wound, and an exit wound on her right check?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I think you've told us that you also saw a statement by an eyewitness to the effect that she was shot in her chest and then she turned and another bullet hit her in the neck and she fell down. Is that correct? That's a statement dated the 25th of February, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You don't have the benefit of the rounds, there is some eyewitness evidence available to you to the effect of where the penetrating wound was and where the exit wound was for one of the two projectiles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had that information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving on to incident number 10. This is the incident where a woman and her daughter, daughter aged eight years, was shot by a single bullet. And you make the point in your report that it would be necessary to determine with precision the angle of entry of the projectile into the bodies, and you would also prefer to have the defined channels of the piercing wounds. Is it the case that when a bullet enters the body that its line of trajectory can change from the point of entry? In other words, in the hypothetical case, where the bullet also exits the body, the trajectory is not necessarily followed, that is, comparing the trajectory before it enters the body with the trajectory in the body.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't fully understood you. What do you mean by "the same trajectory"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not inevitable if it has lost energy. But with regard to this incident, I affirm that it was possible to determine the direction of the shot, but I wasn't precise because I didn't know the exact angle that the projectile came from. What would be interesting in relation to this incident -- what is interesting is that the victim did not hear the shot. That could confirm that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just stop you there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're getting away from the question. The question is: Is it correct that the trajectory is not necessarily maintained when the bullet enters a body, not only because the speed of the bullet is reduced by the denser mass of the body but for other reasons as well?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trajectory in the body is maintained, the same trajectory. It's only the energy that is reduced, and the projectile comes to a halt. If the projectile does not ricochet inside the body, because a projectile does not only ricochet when it encounters an external obstacle. It can ricochet when it hits a bone. I'm not claiming that this is the case in this incident, but that's a possibility. The projectile maintains its trajectory but it is simply slowed down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it not also happen that the bullet loses its shape when it enters a body? Indeed, it can break up?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The deformation of the projectile depends on whether it hit a bone or not. When you examine the projectile, it's possible to "read," it's possible to determine whether the frontal deformation -- whether the front has been deformed or not. But in any event, it's possible for a projectile to be deformed, but this does not necessarily happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if it's deformed, does that not also affect its trajectory?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a very insignificant extent, because the route it travels is not very long. Only if it ricochets because it hits a bone, then the trajectory can change. But when the projectile penetrates a body, the trajectory is not modified to a significant extent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this particular case, where you have a woman and her child aged eight, a reconstruction would have obvious difficulties, would it not, given that they were moving at the time that they were hit, given the age at least of the child?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With regard to the height of the child, only if we took into account the height of the child at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the dependence one would have to place on the recollection of the mother and child as to their precise position at the instant they were shot. Whether they were slightly facing one way or the other, where their limbs were, and so on. Whether they were crouched slightly, if at all, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in relation to incident 11, I think you told us that you drove past that area. And you gave some evidence about this incident on Friday as well. Did you stop and locate the position of the witness as she appeared in the video when she was spoken to by the investigator?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I passed down that street. I saw the surroundings. I watched the video and I saw the photograph of people crossing over. The location was fairly precise, especially since it is probably connected to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just let me stop you. If you could focus on the question. Did you stop and locate the position of the witness as she appeared in the video that we saw on Friday?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And had you seen before that visit two 360-degree photographs, one taken from the position on the road and the other taken from the position above the road?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see those two 360-degree photographs at any stage, either before the visit, during the visit, or after the visit? Have you ever seen them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 360-degree photographs? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two of them.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it was one or two, but I saw the photographs and the 360-degree photographs, and everything that the Defence provided. I saw that on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you --

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a professional point of view, I was interested in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you went there, did you walk up the embankment and look around the area above the embankment in the direction that the witness can be seen on the video pointing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I identified the incidents and the part of the streets they happened in, but I don't remember examining the photographs and then going to the site again because the methodology was not such that one proceeded in this way and there wasn't enough time either --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting your answer, but I'm interested in specifically whether or not you walked up the embankment and looked at the area above the embankment that we can see on the video. Did you or did you not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area above, in the direction of Ozrenska Ulica -- yes, I was in Ozrenska Street and the other streets, but I didn't climb up the embankments, as you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did you say Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ozrenska Street, yes, if we're talking about incident number 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, incident number 11.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking about incident number 10 all the time, because I thought that you had mentioned incident number 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did. And then I thought I mentioned incident number 11. I'm asking you about the incident for which we saw the video on Friday when you were asked questions by Mr. Piletta-Zanin. All right. Now, did you -- you told us this morning that you drove past that area. Yes or no, did you go stop and locate the position where the witness can be seen on the video?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, because that was a large area and it was simply not possible to identify it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I suggest to you there were two ways you could have identified it. One way was by locating the approximate position according to the buildings which appeared in the video and then looking for those buildings as you drove along that street. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't agree with you, because we really needed assistance. If it was so difficult to find the location where the incident was, well, we didn't have any other possibility, let alone the possibility of carrying out such investigations in Sarajevo, given that we didn't have any -- we didn't have authorisation and we weren't escorted either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would have been a relatively simple matter as you drove along that street to identify the area from the images on the video, I suggest to you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe what the witness says, that it was somewhere in that area. If the witness can't identify the position of the victim, then I can only --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, I'm asking you at this stage about identifying where the witness stood as she appeared on the video, that part of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like the witness to be able to answer the question because he was just saying what he could identify and what he couldn't identify, and I think that the witness is being interrupted a little too frequently when he is answering questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Kunjadic, I noticed several times that your answers, although perhaps on very relevant matters, did not correspond completely with what you were asked. May I invite you to listen carefully to the questions. And if, for example, someone asked, did you go on the embankment, then first answer that question. And if you think it's of great importance to tell us what else places you did go, you always can ask me whether you could add something. But perhaps first concentrate specifically on what you're asked. It might be that the next question would invite you to tell us about what you had in mind already. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to be more precise, at line 43 -- sorry, line 7, page 43 the witness was answering why he thought he couldn't identify the position and he was then interrupted. So I think that he should be allowed to continue with his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look again. The question there was about the exact position of the witness. The answer was about what the witness said as to the position of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. victim. Therefore, Mr. Ierace was entitled to interrupt because the answer was not about what he asked the witness, and that's what I pointed out in my observation. Perhaps one of the next questions would be about the position of the victim; I do not know. But certainly Mr. Ierace was allowed to interrupt at this very moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you drove along that road, who was in the vehicle with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, because I went to Sarajevo on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it only the once that you drove along that road?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen before you drove along the road the video that we saw in court on Friday?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I went there before the video was made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a member of the Defence legal team with you in the car, either Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin wasn't with me for sure, but Mrs. Pilipovic was probably present. She was with me on each occasion I went to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand that there was a GPS reading taken of the relevant sites?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there any attempt to use those GPS readings to locate sites?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think it was necessary to locate that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Leaving aside GPS, if you didn't use the image on the video, it would have been impossible to locate where the witness was at the time of the incident, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have located the place if I'd gone to Sarajevo on the basis of the video. But I said that I didn't go to Sarajevo to verify which position the witness was in the street -- which position the witness was in in the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recollect what appears on the two electric 360-degree photographs, the two computerised images?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to incident number 11?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the area that you can see in the video, and down below you can see a slope. The street -- the road descends. I can't remember the details, the houses, or the part of town concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it because you didn't stop that you didn't walk around the area above the embankment in the direction that the woman was seen to be pointing on the video. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, that you have seen the video, do you accept it's possible to drive along the road, identify approximately where the woman was standing, look for the yellow marking that we saw made on the video, walk up the embankment, look around that area, and compare it to a 360-degree photograph taken from the top of the embankment? All that is possible, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am in doubt now. Are we still speaking about incident number 11?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have no reason to believe that we talk about anything else other than incident number 11. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it, Dr. Kunjadic, that you in your last answers, you were thinking about incident 11. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. I do not see that there was any reason to take the view that we are not talking about incident 11 at this very moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now move to incident number 13, Dr. Kunjadic. This is the incident where a boy aged 16 years was shot whilst travelling with his father in a truck close to the present site of the UN field office in Sarajevo. In your report, you mention a projectile that fragmented, and then you have in brackets "(in fact, fragments flew in different directions under the steering wheel so that the damaged --" and then you mention the victim -- "was wounded in the neck by them.)" If I could just firstly clarify something. Are you suggesting that the fragments which wounded the boy in the neck first went under the steering wheel or not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say "fragments," what I mean is that fragments defragmented from the point of impact. And from the point of impact, they then dispersed radially, into different directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. But are you saying that the fragments that hit the boy in the neck first travelled under the steering wheel or are you not saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KUNJADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.
